issues.description:
Element: class name and top-level file structure for Farm.
Problem statement / UML: declares a class Farm with a private List<Animal> animals and public methods addAnimal(Animal), singFarmSong(), feedAllAnimals(), plus a no-arg constructor initializing the list (see UML and tasks). 
Template repository: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a class named AnimalFarm (not Farm), contains duplicated package declarations and malformed nested class/method blocks and TODOs that produce invalid Java source which will not compile. The template's file-level structure and identifier (AnimalFarm) conflict with the expected class name Farm and expected field/method signatures. 
Solution repository: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java provides a correct Farm class with private List<Animal> animals, a no-arg constructor initializing new ArrayList<>(), getters/setters, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), and singFarmSong() that iterates the animals. 
How this blocks students: The template's incorrect class name and malformed file make compilation impossible and prevent students from implementing or testing the intended Farm API, causing confusion about the required class name, fields, and method signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the contents of src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java in the template with a properly formed Farm class skeleton that matches the UML and the solution: declare 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' once at the top; import java.util.List and java.util.ArrayList; declare 'public class Farm' (not AnimalFarm); add a private field 'private List<Animal> animals;'; provide a public no-argument constructor that sets 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>()'; add public methods 'public void addAnimal(Animal animal)', 'public void feedAllAnimals()', and 'public void singFarmSong()' as stubs; and add public getter and setter for animals. Remove duplicate package lines, nested/duplicated class declarations, and any malformed nesting so the file compiles and students can implement the remaining behavior.

issues.description: Concept: the Farm class representing the farm that holds Animal instances. Problem statement (UML and tasks) refers to a class named 'Farm'. The solution repository defines the public class 'Farm' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java at line 6). The template repository's file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java instead declares a public class named 'AnimalFarm' (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java at line 3). This naming mismatch prevents students from mapping the required 'Farm' concept to the provided template, causes compilation errors (file name Farm.java vs public class AnimalFarm), and blocks following the instructions and using Main or tests that reference 'Farm'.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, rename the public class 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' so the public class name matches the file name and the problem statement. Ensure any internal references or comments that mention 'AnimalFarm' are updated accordingly. Alternatively, if keeping 'AnimalFarm', rename the file to match that class and update the problem statement and Main/tests to use the same identifier — but best is to rename the template class to 'Farm' to match the specification and solution.
